issues.description: SealSaloon.acceptSupplyDelivery parameter list is inconsistent: the problem statement/UML specifies acceptSupplyDelivery(String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity), but the solution implements acceptSupplyDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity) (missing the supplierName parameter and the separate ingredientName parameter). This makes it unclear what students should implement and can break tests written against the specification.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the method signature across specification and code. Prefer updating SealSaloon to: public static void acceptSupplyDelivery(String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity). If supplierName is not needed, keep it as an unused parameter but include it to match the spec/tests.

issues.description: Stock API mismatch vs UML/spec: the UML lists Stock methods add, take, findStockIngredient, addToStockIngredients, emptyStock, but the template/solution also expose a public setStockIngredients(StockIngredient[]) method that is not described. This adds an undocumented mutator that students may rely on and conflicts with the stated goal of following the diagram and adding getters for private fields.
issues.suggestedFix: Either add setStockIngredients(StockIngredient[]) to the UML/spec as an allowed helper for setup/testing, or remove it from the template/solution and adapt any setup code/tests to use addToStockIngredients instead.
